375812.title: Erdős–Graham conjecture on monochromatic Pythagorean triples
375812.literal_statement:
A finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ is a colouring with finitely many colours. A **Pythagorean triple** is a triple $(x,y,z)\in\mathbb{N}^3$ satisfying $x^2+y^2=z^2$, and it is monochromatic when all three entries have the same colour.

**Erdős–Graham conjecture.** Any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ has a monochromatic Pythagorean triple.

The necessary direction is not at issue: the conjecture asserts the existence of such a triple for every finite colouring. The paper describes this problem as remaining unsolved and establishes a special case using completely multiplicative functions.

361909.title: Dallard et al.'s equivalence conjecture for tree-independence number
361909.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a hereditary graph class. A graph class is **$(\mathsf{tw},\omega)$-bounded** if its treewidth is bounded by a function of its clique number, and it has **bounded tree-independence number** if the tree-independence numbers of its graphs are uniformly bounded. **Dallard et al.'s conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{G}$ is $(\mathsf{tw},\omega)$-bounded if and only if $\mathcal{G}$ has bounded tree-independence number. Bounded tree-independence number is known to imply $(\mathsf{tw},\omega)$-boundedness, and the converse remains open in general; it is established for several important graph classes.

362991.title: Bergelson–McCutcheon’s non-commuting Schur conjecture
362991.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a group whose centralizer subgroup for every element has infinite index; call such a group **sufficiently non-commutative**. Suppose that $G$ is finitely colored. **Bergelson–McCutcheon’s conjecture.** There exist $x,y\in G$ such that $\{x,y,xy,yx\}$ is monochromatic and

$$
xy\neq yx.
$$

This conjecture is part of the non-commutative analogue of Schur’s theorem, asking for multiplicative configurations in a finite coloring of a sufficiently non-commutative group. The supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.

358902.title: Lovász–Mason flat-condition conjecture for matroid symmetric powers
358902.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with ground set $E$, let $(M_1,\dots,M_d)$ be a symmetric quasi power of $M$, and let $\sF(M)$ denote the set of flats of $M$. For each $F\in\sF(M)$, write $F\cdot\operatorname{Sym}_{d-1}(E)$ for the corresponding subset of the ground set of $M_d$. **Lovász–Mason flat-condition conjecture.** If

$$
F\cdot\operatorname{Sym}_{d-1}(E)\in\sF(M_d)
$$

for every $F\in\sF(M)$, then $M_d$ has rank

$$
\binom{\operatorname{rk}(M)+d-1}{d}.
$$

This is the reverse direction of the implication from the symmetric-power axioms to the flat condition proposed by Mason. The implication from the stronger symmetric-power axiomatization to the flat condition is proved in the paper, but the converse remains open despite substantial effort; the problem was left open by Lovász and Mason.

360514.title: Graham's boundedness conjecture for Euclidean Ramsey sets

360786.title: List-recoverability conjecture for Reed–Solomon codes over prime fields
360786.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be a prime field. Let $\ell \in \mathbb N$ and $\epsilon > 0$ be constants. For each $x \in \mathbb{F}_p$, let $S_x \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ satisfy $|S_x| \leq \ell$.

**Reed–Solomon list-recoverability conjecture.** The number of polynomials $P(X) \in \mathbb{F}_p[X]$ satisfying

$$
\deg(P) \leq (1-\epsilon)p
$$

and

$$
P(x) \in S_x \quad\text{for every }x \in \mathbb{F}_p
$$

is at most $p^{O_{\epsilon,\ell}(1)}$.

This conjecture asserts polynomially bounded list size for the relevant list-recovery instance of Reed–Solomon codes when the evaluation field is prime. The paper notes that results of Guruswami and Rudra imply that the prime-field assumption cannot simply be removed; the conjecture remains open in the stated generality.

373057.title: Roberson's homomorphism-counting conjecture for proper minor-closed classes
373057.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a graph class that is proper, minor-closed, and union-closed. For graphs $G$ and $H$, write $G =_{\mathcal{M}} H$ when $\hom(K,G)=\hom(K,H)$ for every $K\in\mathcal{M}$. **Roberson's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{M}$ is a proper, minor-closed, and union-closed graph class, then there are non-isomorphic graphs $G$ and $H$ such that

$$
G =_{\mathcal{M}} H.
$$

This conjecture says that homomorphism counts from any such proper minor-closed class do not characterize graphs up to isomorphism. The source attributes it to Roberson; its resolution is not specified here.

382165.title: The minimal-class conjecture for sparse hereditary graph classes
382165.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a sparse hereditary class of graphs with unbounded tree-width. A hereditary graph class is **minimal of unbounded tree-width** if it has unbounded tree-width, while every proper hereditary subclass has bounded tree-width. **Minimal-class conjecture.** The class $\mathcal{C}$ does not contain a minimal class of unbounded tree-width. The preceding results establish this for hereditary classes of bounded vertex degree, classes with an excluded minor, and the path-star hereditary classes $\mathcal{R}^{\nu}$, $\mathcal{R}^{\kappa(q)}$ and $\mathcal{R}^{\eta}$; whether it holds for all sparse hereditary classes remains open.

375328.title: Abrishami–Czyżewska–Kluk–Pilipczuk–Pilipczuk–Rzążewski coarse separator conjecture
375328.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For $r\in\mathbb{N}$, an **$r$-cover** of a set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a set $\hat{S}\subseteq V(G)$ such that $S\subseteq N^r_G[\hat{S}]$. A set is **$(k,r)$-coverable** if it has an $r$-cover of size at most $k$. The graph $G$ **admits $(k,r)$-balanced separators** if, for every weight function $w:V(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, it has a $(k,r)$-coverable $w$-balanced separator. A tree decomposition is $(k',r')$-coverable if every bag is $(k',r')$-coverable.

**Abrishami–Czyżewska–Kluk–Pilipczuk–Pilipczuk–Rzążewski's conjecture.** For every $k,r\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $k',r'\in\mathbb{N}$ such that if $G$ admits $(k,r)$-balanced separators, then $G$ admits a $(k',r')$-coverable tree decomposition.

This is proposed as a coarse analogue of the linear correspondence between treewidth and separation number. The converse implication, from a tree decomposition with $(k,r)$-coverable bags to $(k,r)$-balanced separators, follows by a standard argument; the conjectured direction would therefore preserve this correspondence under quasi-isometry.

375918.title: Balister–Győri–Schelp conjecture on Hadamard pair solutions
375918.literal_statement:
Throughout, all vectors and matrices are over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Fix $s\geqslant 2$ and let $M=[v_0,\ldots,v_{2^{s-1}-1}]$ be an $s\times 2^{s-1}$ matrix with nonzero columns. Let $\mathcal{H}=[h_0,\ldots,h_{2^s-1}]$ be an $s\times 2^s$ matrix whose columns are precisely the vectors of $\mathbb{F}_2^s$, each appearing once. A **Hadamard pair solution** for $M$ is an ordering of the columns of $\mathcal{H}$ such that $v_i=h_{2i}+h_{2i+1}$ for every $i\in\{0,\ldots,2^{s-1}-1\}$.

**Balister–Győri–Schelp conjecture.** If

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{2^{s-1}-1}v_i=0,
$$

then $M$ has a Hadamard pair solution.

The zero-sum condition is necessary because the sum of all vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^s$ is zero. The conjecture asserts that this necessary condition is also sufficient for partitioning $\mathbb{F}_2^s$ into pairs with the prescribed nonzero differences; the supplied source does not state whether it has been resolved.

368520.title: The stronger q-analogue of the reverse oddtown theorem
368520.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be an even positive integer and let $F_q^n$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over the finite field with $q$ elements. Write $\mathrm{sub}(F_q^n)$ for its subspaces, and let $[n-1]_q$ denote the $q$-integer. Let $\mathcal{F} \subseteq \mathrm{sub}(F_q^n)$ satisfy that $\dim(A)$ is even for every $A \in \mathcal{F}$ and $\dim(A \cap B)$ is odd for every distinct $A,B \in \mathcal{F}$. **The stronger q-analogue of the reverse oddtown theorem.** If $q$ is an odd prime power, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}| \leq [n-1]_q.
$$

The preceding reverse oddtown q-analogue gives the weaker bound $|\mathcal{F}| \leq [n]_q-1$ when $n$ is even, while the family of codimension-one subspaces inside a fixed $(n-1)$-dimensional subspace has size $[n-1]_q$. The conjecture asserts that this construction is optimal; its status is open based on the information provided.

370387.title: The degeneracy conjecture for proper conflict-free list coloring
370387.literal_statement:
A graph is **$d$-degenerate** if every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree at most $d$. A list assignment $L$ assigns a list of colors $L(v)$ to each vertex $v$; the graph is proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+d)$-choosable if, for every such assignment satisfying $|L(v)|\geq \deg_G(v)+d$ for all vertices $v$, one can choose a color from each list to obtain a proper conflict-free coloring.

**Degeneracy conjecture for proper conflict-free list coloring.** If $G$ is a $d$-degenerate graph for some positive integer $d$, then $G$ is proper conflict-free $({\rm degree}+d)$-choosable.

The statement is motivated by the proved tree case, where the bound is $({\rm degree}+1)$, and by constructions showing that the corresponding bounds cannot generally be lowered. The supplied text gives no evidence that this conjecture has been resolved.

358652.title: Torso-extension equivalence for parameters strictly above treewidth
358652.literal_statement:
Let ${\sf p}:{\mathcal{G}}_{{\text{\, \textsf{all}}}}\to\mathbb{N}$ be a minor-monotone parameter. For an annotated graph $(G,X)$, let ${\sf p}(G,X)$ denote the annotated extension of ${\sf p}$, and define the torso extension by

$$
{\sf p}^{\mathsf{t}}(G,X)=\min\{{\sf p}(\operatorname{torso}(G,Z))\mid X\subseteq Z\subseteq V(G)\}.
$$

Here $\operatorname{torso}(G,Z)$ is obtained by adding all edges between the vertices of $N_G(V(C))$ in $G[Z]$, for every connected component $C$ of $G-Z$, and ${\sf tw}\precnsim {\sf p}$ means that ${\sf p}$ is functionally strictly bigger than treewidth. **Torso-extension equivalence conjecture.** The torso extension and the annotated extension of ${\sf p}$ are equivalent if and only if ${\sf tw}\precnsim {\sf p}$. The conjecture proposes a characterization of when torso-based and annotated extensions coincide for minor-monotone parameters; the preceding discussion notes that the equivalence can fail for treewidth itself, while it is expected for parameters functionally strictly bigger than treewidth.

358002.title: Bergeron's Gaussian-polynomial inequality conjecture
358002.literal_statement:
Let $a,b,c,d$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
0<a\leq b<c\leq d,\qquad ad=bc.
$$

The Gaussian polynomial $\binom{n}{k}_q$ is the $q$-analogue of the binomial coefficient, and $f(q)\geq g(q)$ means that $f(q)-g(q)$ has non-negative coefficients. **Bergeron's conjecture.** The difference

$$
\binom{b+c}{b}_q-\binom{a+d}{a}_q
$$

is symmetric and coefficientwise non-negative. The source presents this as the Gaussian-polynomial consequence of Vessenes' conjecture; it notes that symmetry is clear, while the non-negativity question was the subject of the paper's special cases and was not resolved in general there.

367360.title: Caro's zero-sum Ramsey conjecture for trees modulo 3
367360.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n \equiv 1 \pmod{3}$ vertices. **Caro's conjecture.**

$$
R(T,\mathbb{Z}_3) = \begin{cases} n+2, & \text{if } T \text{ is the star } K_{1,n-1} \\ n+1, & \text{if } T \text{ has no vertex of degree } 0 \pmod{3} \\ n, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}
$$

This conjecture extends the understanding of zero-sum Ramsey numbers from $\mathbb{Z}_2$ to the next cyclic group, $\mathbb{Z}_3$. The source presents it as proposed by Caro in 2019; no resolution is given here.

369938.title: Graham's valid-ordering conjecture over finite prime fields
369938.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be prime. A **valid ordering** of a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p\setminus\{0\}$ is an ordering $g_1,g_2,\ldots,g_n$ of its elements such that the partial sums

$$
g_1,\quad g_1+g_2,\quad g_1+g_2+g_3,\quad \ldots,\quad g_1+\cdots+g_n
$$

are all distinct. **Graham's conjecture.** Every subset of $\mathbb{F}_p\setminus\{0\}$ admits a valid ordering. This is the simplest instance of the paper's broader question about valid orderings of subsets of groups, and was first posed by Graham in 1971 and later reiterated by Erdős and Graham; it remains open according to the supplied status evidence.
